chapter: Recollections of Trent's band and its influence
title: Sy Oliver in Trent's band and writing high trombone parts
summary: Sy Oliver joined after the fire; he wrote Mosley's parts very high, which pushed him upward.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Sy told me that when he joined your band--Trent's band, that was in the time when morale was bad, right after that fire--
Right.
They lost all the instruments, so the morale was bad then. He said Trent must have been something at one time, but they weren't anything when I was with them.
I saw one of the articles that he wrote and he said it was one of the greatest things he ever heard.
That's funny, he didn't say that.
I got the book here.
I know the book you're talking about.
It seems strange.
He said that I was a guiding light. I was surprised too because we used to fight like cats and dogs.
I imagine; yeah. I know he was a fighting kind of guy.
That was the reason that I play as high as I do on the trombone today, because--Sy never could play very much trumpet--
No, I know he wasn't, he was a fair trumpet player.
He was very fair and he was a wonderful arranger and I used to tell him that.
Didn't he try to write-- wasn't he always trying to write along that kind of two beat style even way back then?
Yeah.
And that wasn't Trent's
style really. Trent was really a four-four style and it was all accent.

The thing of it is to out do me he would write my parts way up high, so I was determined not to let this guy laugh at me and I'd go ahead and make them as high as he--I seen him put them up to G, E flat, even if they're F and I made that F; scared him to death. It scared me when I first saw it.
Yeah, I can imagine, because the trombone was playing up like that.
But I got up there and I started liking playing up there and I started liking the execution up there.
